-3-  NC: 2025:KHC-K:6521-DB  MFA No. 201854 of 2024 HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT
(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD)

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the claimants being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 12.09.2023 passed by the MACT and III Additional Senior Civil Judge, Kalaburagi, in MVC No.851/2020.
2.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 10.11.2019 at about 7.50 p.m.,
the deceased Madhusudan Reddy was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/E-8012 near Gumpa Gate, on Ganganpalli to Bhaktampalli main road.
At that time, a lorry bearing registration No.MH-10/Z-3309 was parked in the middle of the road without any parking lights, parking signals or fencing of stones placed by its side.
As the deceased did not notice the parked lorry, dashed the lorry to its rear end side.
As a result, he fell NC: 2025:KHC-K:6521-DB HC-KAR down from the motorcycle, sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased Madhusudan Reddy along with interest.
4. On service of summons, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through their respective counsel.
Respondent No.1 did not choose to file any statement of objections.
Respondent No.2 filed his written statement, specifically and categorically denying the contents of the petition.
He also denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased.

It was contended that the concerned police had filed a charge sheet against both the driver of the lorry and the deceased rider of the motorcycle, and therefore, there was contributory negligence on the part of the deceased in causing the accident.

It was further contended that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident, and though the offending lorry was insured with respondent NC:
2025:KHC-K:6521-DB HC-KAR No.2, the policy conditions had been violated.
Hence, respondent No.2 sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.

The claimants in order to prove the case, examined claimant No.1 as PW.1 Manimala And Ors vs Veerappa And Anr on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18052183/
3 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On behalf of the respondents, respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
6.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of the rash and negligent acts of both the driver of the lorry and the rider of the motorcycle.
As a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to only 50% of the total compensation of Rs.27,04,300/-
from respondent Nos.1 and 2, along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., and directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to deposit only 50% of the NC: 2025:KHC-K:6521-DB HC-KAR entire compensation amount along with interest within 90 days from the date of passing of the award.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment, the present appeal has been filed.

7. Sri. Nagraj Patil, learned counsel appearing for the claimants has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the lorry, who had parked the lorry in the middle of the road.

The Tribunal erred in fastening 50%
of the liability on the deceased, which is contrary to the material available on record.
In support of his case, he has also relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Archit Saini Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., 2018 SC 1143.

entities.text: Archit Saini Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., 2018 SC 1143
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: b) Secondly, it was further contended that the driver of the lorry had parked the vehicle in the middle of the road at about 7.50 p.m., during the night, without switching on any indicator or any parking lights.
As a NC: 2025:KHC-K:6521-DB HC-KAR result, the rider of the motorcycle was unable to notice the parked lorry in the night.
Hence, the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the driver of the lorry, which resulted in the death of the motorcycle rider.
The Tribunal erred in holding that the deceased had contributed 50% to the occurrence of the accident.
c) Lastly, in respect of quantum, it was contended that, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal.

8. On the other hand, Smt. Sangeeta Bhadrashetty, learned counsel appearing for the Respondent No.2-Insurance Company has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the accident occurred due to the negligence of deceased as well as the driver of the lorry.
Even though the lorry had been parked on the road, there was sufficient space for the rider of the motorcycle to NC: 2025:KHC-K:6521-DB HC-KAR pass.
However, the rider of the motorcycle was driving in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the parked lorry.
The Tribunal, after considering the evidence on record, has rightly answered Issue No.1 Partly Affirmative.

4 b)

sentences.text: Secondly, in respect of quantum of compensation, she has contended that considering the evidence of the parties, as well as the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the appeal.
9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
10. The case of the claimants is that on 10.11.2019, at about 7.50 p.m., the deceased Madhusudan Reddy was driving the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/E-8012.

When he reached near Gumpa Gate, on the Ganganpalli to Bhaktampalli main road, a lorry bearing registration No.MH-10/Z-3309 was NC: 2025:KHC-K:6521-DB HC-KAR parked in the middle of the road without any parking light.
The deceased, not seeing the parked lorry, dashed the lorry and fell down from the motorcycle, sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
11. The police registered an FIR and abated charge sheet against the deceased and the driver of the lorry.
As per the sketch, the width of the road is about 24 feet.
The lorry was parked about 10 feet from the side of the road.
There was sufficient space left towards the right side of the lorry for the vehicles to pass coming from opposite direction.
12. Since the accident occurred at about 7.50 pm., night, the lorry which was parked in the middle of the road without any parking light and the rider of the motorcycle was unable to see it.

Although,
there was sufficient space on the left side to pass through, the rider was traveling at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the parked lorry.

Considering the evidence of the parties, the spot mahazar, the sketch, the FIR and the - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6521-DB HC-KAR charge sheet, we are of the opinion that both the driver of the lorry and the rider of the motorcycle were negligent in causing the accident.
The deceased contributed 20% to the accident, while the driver of the lorry contributed 80%.
To that extent, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal are modified.
13. In respect of quantum is concerned, considering the age and avocation of the deceased and the evidence of PW.1, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

14. Accordingly, we pass the following order:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The Judgment and award of the Claims Tribunal is modified.

iii) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit only 80% of the total compensation of Rs.27,04,300/-

 iv) The apportionment, deposit and  release of amount shall be made in  terms of the award of the Tribunal.
